title: Donor Liver split for two adult Recipients with DHOPE
summary:
Liver transplantation is the only curative treatment option for many advanced liver diseases and certain tumors.
However, due to a severe and persistent shortage of donor organs, this treatment option is limited. This ultimately led to the expansion of the donor pool and the increasing acceptance of organs with extended donor criteria, such as advanced donor age or high donor BMI, or even mild fatty liver disease. These are not reasons to reject a donor organ. Despite these extended criteria, an organ can be transplanted safely and with good results; the risk of complications is low, and, especially in critically ill patients, prompt liver transplantation usually remains the only chance for a cure.
Due to the shortage of donor organs and the donor's own risk factors, a method for optimizing organ preservation was approved for use in Germany in 2022: machine perfusion.
After removal of the donor organ, it is transported to the recipient center and then flushed with a special, oxygen-enriched solution.
Machine perfusion has been proven to reduce the risk of complications after liver transplantation. To increase the availability of donor organs, it is possible to divide donor livers. This is currently performed for one adult and one child, provided the donor quality is very good. Dividing a donor liver for two adults is not yet a routine procedure. However, the availability of machine perfusion now makes it possible to assess and divide the donor liver under continuous machine perfusion. This makes it possible to transplant two adults with one donor liver. This shortens the waiting list time and thus the risk of tumor progression or withdrawal from the waiting list due to poor general health.
conditions: Alcoholic fibrosis and sclerosis of liver
Malignant neoplasm: Intrahepatic bile duct carcinoma
Malignant neoplasm: Other sarcomas of liver

interventions.name: The indication and listing for liver transplantation are determined at the respective study center following a decision by the transplantation conference and the guidelines for waiting list management and organ allocation pursuant to Section 16 (1) Sentence 1 Nos. 2 and 5 of the Transplantation Act

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Donor Selection
• Age ≤ 65 years
• Fatty liver disease ≤ 30% (macrovesicular, biopsy if necessary)
• No liver fibrosis
• No liver cirrhosis
• Serum sodium ≤ 160 mg/dL
• ICU time ≤ 5 days
• Transaminases no more than 5 times the normal values
• Cold ischemia time < 10 h
• Body weight ≥ 60 kg

- Recipient Selection
• Age ≥ 18 years
• Indication for liver transplantation
• Listing for liver transplantation
• Consent to the study
Exclusion criteria:
Donor
• Liver fibrosis
• Liver cirrhosis
• Age > 65 years
• Serum sodium > 160 mg/dL
• ICU > 5 days
• Transaminases higher than 5 times the normal values
• Cold ischemia time ≥ 10 h
• Body weight < 60 kg

- Recipient
• Human liver status
• Age < 18 years
• Contraindications to liver transplantation according to the Federal Medical Association's Guidelines
• No consent to the study
